name: Processor D
justification: The primary bottleneck measured on Processor A for the N=4 ring TFIM Trotter circuit is routing overhead: A lacks a 4-qubit cycle so SABRE inserts SWAPs (each costing 3 CX gates), inflating two-qubit gate counts and depth significantly. Processor D is designed as a double-ring (two concentric 4-cycles: 0-1-2-3-0 and 4-5-6-7-4, with spokes 0-4, 1-5, 2-6, 3-7), giving every pair of ring qubits direct connectivity at graph distance at most 2. The N=4 ring bonds (0,1),(1,2),(2,3),(3,0) embed directly onto the inner ring with zero SWAPs needed, eliminating the dominant noise source on Processor A. The design accepts the same official noise rates (p1=0.001, p2=0.005, p_readout=0.01), since lower rates are not permitted. The trade-off is using 8 qubits instead of 5 (A) to achieve the SWAP-free 4-cycle embedding, increasing physical qubit cost but substantially reducing routing-induced CX overhead and improving fidelity at all Trotter step counts.
